newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela ups spending plans on wage deal.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela ups spending plans on wage deal.

text.p: The Venezuelan government has upped its spending plans for 1997 to as much as 7.5 trillion bolivars ($15.9 billion) from 7.2 trillion due to pending public sector salary increases, a government official said.
"We're revising the target due to salary increases," Finance vice minister Wilmer Perez, told reporters.

The new level falls within the maximum 7.8 trillion bolivars budget for the year and Perez said "it would not have an inflationary impact ... as it will be financed with internal resources and other spending cuts".
On Wednesday, Venezuela's tax authority Seniat said January tax collection was 17 percent ahead of targets at 304 billion bolivars.

Last week, the government offered public sector workers a 35 percent salary increase plus a 50 percent increase in bonuses. Government sources said total funds earmarked for public sector salaries in the 1997 budget were 1.25 trillion bolivars.
